messages:
Alex: Heads up — flight's delayed, looks like I'm going to miss the first 90m of my primary window. Sorry y'all.
Sam: ack. Are you able to hand off now or want us to stand up a temporary secondary?
Alex: I'm at the gate, terminal B. Might not get solid wifi for another 30m. Can @Priya or @Morgan take primary until I get online? I can shadow when I land.
Priya: I can step in for the next 2h. Quick check — is there anything on the watchlist right now?
Alex: Thanks Priya. Main risk is the inference rpc latency spike we saw earlier — pages were low but customer facing UI slow. Runbook link: https://internal.runbooks/redwood/latency-rpc (cc @incident-bot)
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: service=inference-runtime severity=warning count=3 in last 10m — escalation policy=primary-first. Escalation target: @Alex (primary).
Sam: Ok incident-bot noted. Priya, two quick things: 1) check /dash/runtime/latency for the 95th pct, 2) tail the logs for model-router pods with `kubetool logs -f model-router -n prod | grep -i slow`.
Priya: On it. Running the query now. 95p is 620ms, baseline 200-250ms. Seeing a correlated queue depth bump on the batcher.
Morgan: If queue depth is up, consider temporarily lowering max_batch_size on canary pool. Command snippet: ```kubectl patch configmap batcher-config -n prod --patch '{"data":{"max_batch_size":"8"}}'``` — that'll reduce throughput but keep latency tighter.
Priya: Good call. Before we patch, what's the SLA impact on high-QPS tenants? 
Alex: (via DM) For a short 30-60m patch, major tenants degrade throughput but UI latency improves. Prefer we do it if 95p stays >500ms.
Sam: Priya — you have permission to apply that patch. If you do, leave a quick note in this thread. Also set a reminder to revert after 1h.
Priya: Applying patch now. Patching... ✅ Patch applied at 2026-03-15T02:10Z.
incident-bot: Deploy event: config-update/batcher-config by Priya — status=success — duration=12s
Priya: Seeing 95p drop to 310ms within two minutes. Queue depth steady. Will monitor for 15m.
Alex: Thanks Priya — huge help. I'm on airplane wifi, will be reachable but slow. If anything escalates, @Sam please take over primary.
Sam: Roger. Priya — can you also start a short perf capture and upload to the incident channel? Command: `perf-collect --service inference-runtime --minutes 5 --output /tmp/perf.tgz`
Priya: Running perf collect now. Uploading when done.
Morgan: Tagging runbook snippets for future: latency runbook §3 (batcher knobs) + emergency fallback model variant. Saved here: https://internal.docs/redwood/latency#batcher-knobs
Sam: Ok we have temporary coverage plan: Priya primary, Sam secondary, Alex shadowing. I'll update the oncall rotation calendar to reflect the temporary swap and set the reminder to revert the config. :thumbsup:
Priya: perf upload done at 2026-03-15T02:18Z -> https://artifacts/redwood/perf/4112223334-perf.tgz
incident-bot: Alert cleared: service=inference-runtime — current severity=info — reason=95p latency back within target
Sam: Nice work. Priya, please leave the patch for now and we'll revert after the 1h watch if stable. Alex, safe travels — ping if you want to retake primary when landed.
Alex: Thanks everyone. Really appreciate the quick coverage.
Priya: np. I'll post a brief blurb in the rotation thread when I hand back.
Sam: Closing loop: I'll mark the temporary handoff in the oncall sheet and set a calendar event for revert at 2026-03-15T03:10Z.
Morgan: Noted. If anything spikes again, escalate to SEV2 per runbook.
Alex: Logged. Thanks all :pray:
